podcast.title: Assault by Jack White
podcast.body: In December 2003, Jason Stollsteimer was allegedly assaulted by Jack White at The Magic Stick club in Detroit during a record release party. White, who had previously produced an album for The Von Bondies and invited them to open for The White Stripes, reportedly became enraged after Stollsteimer brushed him off, leading to White allegedly punching him multiple times and spitting on him. "This happened at a club called the Magic Stick where Jason was at a record release party for another band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Detroit Origins and White Stripes Connection
podcast.body: The Von Bondis were also from Detroit and had a fluctuating relationship with The White Stripes, sometimes as friends, rivals, or enemies. The band's main members were Jason Stolstheimer, a bartender, and Marcy Bowen, who worked in a hair salon. They started as The Baby Killers in 1997, changing their name to The Von Bondis by 2000, and were signed by Sympathy for the Record Industry, similar to The White Stripes. "They were also from Detroit, and were alternately friends and rivals and enemies of the White Stripes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Jack White's Conviction for Assault
podcast.body: Following the incident, Jack White pleaded guilty to aggravated assault, was fined $750, and ordered to attend an anger management course. "In the end, Jack pleaded guilty to aggravated assault. He was fined $750 and told to take an anger management course."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: UK Success and Jack White Co-Production
podcast.body: Like The White Stripes and The Strokes, The Von Bondis initially found significant attention in the UK. They toured with The White Stripes and other young Garage Rock bands, and Jack White notably co-produced their first album, "Lack of Communication." "It just like the Stripes in the Strokes, the first territory to pay close attention was the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Assault on Jason Stollsteimer of The Von Bondies
xref.body: In December 2003, Jack White was involved in an altercation with Jason Stollsteimer of The Von Bondies at The Magic Stick club in Detroit during a record release party. Reportedly, after being brushed off by Stollsteimer, White allegedly pinned him against speaker stacks, yelled at him, and when Stollsteimer didn't respond, allegedly threw him to the ground, punched him seven times in the face, and spat on him. It took several people to pull White away. This was particularly "weird" as Jack White had previously helped The Von Bondies by producing an album for them and inviting them to open for The White Stripes. "The story is that Jack tried to speak with Jason but was brushed off. Some say Jack pin Jason against the speaker stacks and started yelling."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
